title: Preparation and characterization of a self‐assembled peptide gel from enzymatic hydrolysis of edible bird's nest
content:
Abstract

BACKGROUND

Large quantities of edible bird's nest (EBN) fragments are generated during processing, and their fragmented appearance limits consumer acceptance. The poor water solubility of EBN also restricts the use of these fragments. We previously observed that EBN became soluble and then gelled when an EBN suspension was hydrolyzed by neutral protease. Thus, this study prepared and characterized such an EBN peptide gel.

RESULTS

Specifically, a 0.090 g g−1 EBN suspension was hydrolyzed by neutral protease (120 U g−1 EBN) for 36 h. EBN was completely dissolved in water after hydrolysis for 20 min, and the solution became gelled after hydrolysis for 4 h. After 24 h, the gel strength reached the maximum value. Transmission electron microscopy analysis demonstrated that EBN hydrolysates from different durations aggregated into fibrils, and the size was positively correlated with the hydrolysis duration. Moreover, the α-helix content increased as the hydrolysis duration increased, and peptides with molecular weight between 8 and 20 kDa became predominant. These findings suggested that α-helix-rich hydrolysates in this size range contributed to self-assembly and gelation. In addition, phenylalanine was the most abundant free amino acid from hydrolysis of EBN, which might also contribute to gelation.

CONCLUSION

This work provides an innovative approach to utilize EBN fragments and enrich the type of the EBN product. © 2026 Society of Chemical Industry.
